verdict.rationale: Flagsmith documents first-party self-hosting, including Docker and Kubernetes/Helm deployments, explicitly framed as data sovereignty: users keep feature flag data in their own infrastructure and so choose where it lives. The evidence does not show a region or residency choice for the managed cloud service, so residency control depends on running the platform yourself. Missing for 10: selectable data-storage regions (e.g. EU/US) for the hosted SaaS, documentation of managed-cloud residency guarantees, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: **Data sovereignty**: Keep your feature flag data within your own infrastructure
Self-hosting Flagsmith allows you to run the complete Flagsmith platform within your own infrastructure, giving you full control over your data, security policies, and deployment environment.
Kubernetes and OpenShift: Full Kubernetes deployment with Helm charts and operators
